title: Network nonlocality with tripartite entangled sources
abstract: Quantum networks are built from independent sources, and their nonlocality has mostly been studied with sources that emit bipartite entangled states. A source of three entangled qubits is richer, since its nonlocality can be tested by the Mermin or the more demanding Svetlichny inequality. We ask how network nonlocality relates to these two single-source notions and find that the answer depends on the wiring. When two central nodes without inputs share every source, Bell-state measurements turn every Svetlichny violation into a network violation, and even all entangled generalised Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger states violate the network inequality. When a single central node is shared, the relation reverses, and a network violation requires a Mermin violation of the source. With more sources, the maximal violation depends on whether their number is even or odd, and we give tight bounds for both cases. These results show that the way multipartite sources are wired decides which kind of nonlocality a network inherits.
summary: This theoretical work explores the relationship between network nonlocality and single-source nonlocality in quantum networks using tripartite entangled sources. It demonstrates that the specific physical wiring of the network dictates which type of nonlocality violation (Mermin or Svetlichny) is necessary or sufficient for the network to exhibit nonclassical correlations. This has implications for designing robust quantum communication channels.
main_problem: The paper investigates how network nonlocality, generated by independent sources emitting tripartite entangled states, relates to single-source nonlocality measures like Mermin and Svetlichny inequalities.
main_result: The relationship between network nonlocality and single-source nonlocality depends critically on the network wiring: a closed network structure implies a Svetlichny violation leads to a network violation, while an open network requires a Mermin violation.
method: The authors analyze network nonlocality by comparing correlation tensors derived from different network topologies (closed vs. open) against established single-source bounds using inequalities.
model_or_system: The model involves quantum networks built from independent sources emitting three-qubit entangled states, with the nonlocality tested across different network architectures (wirings).

important_parameters: The number of sources (odd vs. even) and the specific network wiring (closed vs. open).
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on comparing network nonlocality to single-copy tests and is restricted to simple wiring configurations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate various network topologies (closed/open) using tripartite sources, and tables compare the derived nonlocality values against local bounds.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares network nonlocality derived from different wiring schemes (closed vs. open) against the bounds set by single-source entanglement tests (Mermin and Svetlichny), deriving specific mathematical relationships for each case.
why_interesting: It provides a deep structural understanding of how multipartite entanglement resources are utilized and constrained when distributed across a network architecture, which is fundamental to quantum communication protocols.
